milestone_brief:
textbook-ingest-m12 — notebook_textbook_ingest driver: embed m7 textbook chunk JSONs and write them into a notebook's LanceDB so textbook chunks are retrievable via search_papers. Closes the e4 OUTCOME end-to-end (the "Milne/Caraiani PDFs return in search_papers result rows" demo) and the follow-up tracked at chris-dare-dev/arXMCP#8.

CONTEXT / VERIFIED CURRENT STATE (from a scoping pass):
- chunk_textbook(slug, paper_id) -> list[ChunkRecord] (ingest/textbook_chunker.py) ALREADY produces the textbook chunks AND writes per-chunk JSONs to <nb_dir>/chunks/<flat_paper_id>/. Its module docstring (line ~43) states it "Writes chunk JSONs only — NOT LanceDB. Embedding/LanceDB-write is a [follow-up]." That follow-up IS this milestone.
- The arXiv embed->write seam is: embed_paper(paper_id) (ingest/embedder.py:889) writes an NPZ -> load_embed_record(paper_id) (ingest/store.py) -> write_chunks(chunks, embed_record, lancedb_path=...) (ingest/store.py). bulk_ingest.py:309-320 chains these. embed_paper reads chunks from the GLOBAL chunk-store layout keyed by paper_id.
- tools/notebook_ingest.py (212 LOC) is the arXiv notebook orchestration template: it calls run_bulk_ingest with lancedb_staging_path = var/arxmcp/notebooks/<slug>/lancedb, then builds a BM25 index. tools/_notebook_common.py has notebook_dir(slug) + the per-notebook path helpers.
- Per-notebook serving (notebook-retrieval m1/m2): ARXMCP_NOTEBOOK=<slug> (process-level) OR filters.notebook=<slug> (per-call, fork-A m2) serves the per-notebook LanceDB at var/arxmcp/notebooks/<slug>/lancedb. search_papers is dense-only at v1.
- m9 added a WRITE-TIME INVARIANT in ingest/store.write_chunks: the chunk_id prefix must agree with source_kind (textbook: <-> "textbook"). chunk_textbook already emits textbook:<slug>:<hex> chunk_ids + source_kind="textbook", so the driver must preserve these (do NOT trip the invariant).
- m11 added the get_chunk non-OA license-truncation policy (license column drives it). Textbook chunks carry their license token (e.g. GFDL, author-distributed); the driver must write the license column through unchanged (write_chunks already round-trips it).

CENTRAL DESIGN FORK (resolve in research): embed_paper(paper_id) assumes the GLOBAL chunk-store layout, but textbook chunk JSONs live in the NOTEBOOK-scoped <nb_dir>/chunks/<flat_paper_id>/ dir. So the driver must EITHER (a) teach embed_paper / the embedder a textbook (notebook-scoped) chunk-source, OR (b) embed the ChunkRecords that chunk_textbook returns DIRECTLY into an EmbedRecord (lower-level encode, no global-store NPZ round-trip) then write_chunks against the notebook LanceDB path. Pick the option that (i) reuses the BGE-M3 dual-column embedder + its stmt/proof routing rule WITHOUT duplicating it, (ii) keeps the path testable WITHOUT the real model (inject/monkeypatch synthetic embeddings, like tests/test_store.py::_make_synthetic_embeddings), (iii) does not bypass write_chunks' validation (the m9 prefix invariant, the dual-column NPZ-alignment check). Give a concrete recommended shape with file:line anchors + the exact embed entrypoint to reuse.

OPEN QUESTIONS for research to resolve:
- Does the driver take a textbook:<slug> notebook slug only, or (slug, paper_id) pairs? (mirror tools/notebook_ingest.py's CLI.)
- Build a per-notebook BM25 index (as notebook_ingest.py does) or skip it (search_papers is dense-only at v1, so dense suffices for the e4 demo)? Recommend.
- corpus_version: the per-notebook LanceDB has its own MVCC version (starts at 1). Confirm write_chunks + the notebook corpus-version.json marker handle this (mirror notebook_ingest.py's _read_corpus_version).
- Does chunk_textbook need to be CALLED by the driver (chunk -> embed -> write in one pass), or does the driver read pre-written chunk JSONs from disk? Recommend the one-pass shape unless there's a reason to decouple.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A new tools/notebook_textbook_ingest.py that, given a textbook notebook slug (+ paper_id(s)), embeds the textbook chunks and writes them to var/arxmcp/notebooks/<slug>/lancedb via ingest.store.write_chunks (source_kind="textbook", textbook: chunk_ids, license preserved).
- INTEGRATION TEST (model-free, the payoff): write textbook chunks via the driver path using SYNTHETIC embeddings, then query search_papers against that notebook (ARXMCP_NOTEBOOK or filters.notebook) with filters.source_kind="textbook" and assert the textbook chunk is returned. This is the e4-demo-closing regression guard.
- Idempotent re-run (write_chunks merge_insert on chunk_id — no duplicates).
- The m9 prefix<->source_kind invariant is satisfied (textbook chunks write cleanly).
- The embed step reuses the existing BGE-M3 dual-column embedder (no duplicated encode/routing logic); the real-model path may be requires_model-gated, but the write+retrieve wiring is proven model-free.
- corpus_version / per-notebook MVCC handled (mirror notebook_ingest.py).
- No MCP tool-schema change expected (this is an ingest CLI tool, not a server-surface change) -> NO EXPECTED_TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256 / EXPECTED_BP1_SHA256 re-pin (flag if that assumption breaks).

CONSTRAINTS: assert banned for invariants (use if...raise); local-first; no anthropic SDK at runtime; no-fork; doc placement under .claude/. This is an ingest/tools CLI driver (NOT server middleware), so the pure-ASGI / BaseHTTPMiddleware constraints don't apply here.

EXTERNAL WRITES: on success, closing chris-dare-dev/arXMCP#8 is a candidate (Phase-4 per-event-authorized gh operation). The push is separately per-event authorized.
